subject: DTIA / UK Addendum: proposed routing variance and subprocessor notes
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@medintel.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Turner <ben.turner@medintel.com>, legal@medintel.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Initial scope for DTIA/TIA review: MedIntel pilot

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with a small pilot and need to confirm transfer safeguards before legal signs off. Attached is a short workbook with the flows we expect (MedIntel EU customers -> Redwood hosted inference -> third-party analytics). Key asks:

- Which model variants will process EU customer data?
- Can Redwood commit to SCCs + UK IDTA (UK Addendum) where required?
- We need a mapping of subprocessors that will have access to logs/metrics (esp. analytics and observability partners).

Also, are you able to accept a limited routing variance for a 3-month pilot (some inference tokens may be routed to a non-EU region for burst execution)? That will be a blocker for us if it isn't covered by the DTIA/UK Addendum.

I've attached medintel_dtia_scope.xlsx with a proposed flow. Can your team review and call out gaps? Legal@medintel.com is on copy for contract-language comments.

Thanks,
Asha
Asha Rao
Head of Privacy & Compliance
MedIntel Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@medintel.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Turner <ben.turner@medintel.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial scope for DTIA/TIA review: MedIntel pilot

Hi Asha —

Appreciate the detail and the workbook, we reviewed it with infra and legal. High-level response:

- Model variants: hosted inference will run on Redwood-verified open models and you can pin to EU-only model variants; we will share a profile of the model build/quantization and expected token footprint.
- Transfers: we support SCCs today and can execute the UK IDTA + UK Addendum for UK data subjects. For the routing variance you mentioned, we can offer a limited routing exception for burst capacity under specific controls (see proposed mitigations below).
- Subprocessors: we'll provide a subprocessor map (access tiers: live inference, logging/metrics, billing) and an attestation for any non-EU subprocessors.

Proposed mitigations for the 3-month burst routing variance:
1) Routing flagging: all requests eligible for burst will be tagged and logged.
2) Data minimization: prefix/KV caching where possible; do not persist full transcripts for bursted requests.
3) Contractual fallback: if a routing event cannot be remediated, Redwood will route back to EU-only capacity and notify within 2 hours.

I'll loop in Kimberly and Marissa to align on the contractual language and the subprocessor list. Would you be available for a 30-minute call Thursday to walk the workbook line-by-line?

Cheers,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: DTIA / UK Addendum: proposed routing variance and subprocessor notes

Folks —

Forwarding Asha's workbook and Soojin's notes. Quick internal checklist before the call with MedIntel:

- Contract: we should offer a DTIA + UK Addendum template but include an explicit routing exception section limited to: duration (90 days), audit rights, logging retention (14 days for burst logs), and irrevocable fallback. Legal wants language that allows us to throttle burst traffic to preserve SLOs.
- Subprocessors: identify which telemetry vendors will see inferred tokens or traces. I think ObservIQ & Metricly are the two partners in scope — Vic (infra) can confirm.
- Data flow model: ensure we can provide per-route tracing so we can show evidence of routing decisions.

Action items:
- Marissa: prepare DPA/UK Addendum draft with a routing variance paragraph and a table of subprocessors (include access tier).
- Vivek: confirm infra controls and whether we can add a header tag for bursted requests; also confirm retention windows.
- Soojin: lead the client call and capture MedIntel's redline expectations.

Thanks — aiming to have a draft to share back by Friday EOD.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
VP, Product & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@medintel.com>

Cc: legal@medintel.com, Ben Turner <ben.turner@medintel.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DTIA / UK Addendum: proposed routing variance and subprocessor notes

Thanks Kimberly — that level of detail helps. A couple of comments from legal after a quick pass:

- Routing variance: MedIntel can accept a temporary routing exception only if the routed payload is pseudonymized (no direct identifiers) and we have a right to audit the logs for any routing events.
- Retention: they want burst logs retained for 90 days (we proposed 14). Can Redwood offer a compromise (30 days) if access is restricted and logs are stored encrypted with customer-scoped keys?
- Subprocessors: legal flagged ObservIQ as a potential concern and asked for subprocessor-specific SOC2/perimeter attestations.

We can discuss on the call but please prepare suggested language for: pseudonymization requirement, minimum retention windows, and an attestation checklist for subprocessors.

Asha
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@medintel.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DTIA / UK Addendum: proposed routing variance and subprocessor notes

Asha / team —

Thanks for the feedback and clear asks. Quick decisions from Redwood side after infra/legal sync:

1) Pseudonymization: we can add a contractual obligation that bursted requests must pass through a client-side pseudonymization step if MedIntel requires it. We'll show the pseudonymization checklist during the pilot onboarding.

2) Retention compromise: Redwood can set burst-log retention to 30 days encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys (KMS integration). We'll add an audit hook that allows MedIntel to request a routing-event dump within 48 hours of an incident.

3) Subprocessor attestations: we will include a subprocessor schedule and attach SOC 2 Type II / ISO27001 evidence for ObservIQ and Metricly where applicable; if MedIntel needs additional attestations we'll work with our partners but may need a 2-week lead time.

Next steps:
- I'll send a short redline for the DTIA/UK Addendum (target: EOD tomorrow).
- Kimberly will include a routing-variance clause and a retention table in the draft.
- Marissa will circulate the subprocessor schedule and evidence pack.

Soojin
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
